subject: READ statement
notes:
RULE: 'If neither the NEXT phrase nor the PREVIOUS phrase is specified and ACCESS MODE SEQUENTIAL is specified in the file control entry for file-name-1, the NEXT phrase is implied.' (cite.py --check 14.9.30.3 OK.)
IMPLEMENTED ON BOTH ARMS. Keyed arm: KeyedIoBinder.BindRead's access-mode switch ends `_ => previous ? KeyedReadKind.Previous : KeyedReadKind.Next` with the comment '14.9.30 SR8 -- sequential access: NEXT implied', and FileAccessMode.Sequential falls to it. Sequential-organization arm: BoundRead is unconditionally a forward read, so NEXT is implied by construction.
PROBED ON ALL THREE ORGANIZATIONS. (a) indexed, ACCESS SEQUENTIAL, two records K001/K002, `MOVE "K002" TO IX-KEY` then two bare `READ IXF RECORD` -> `R1 FS=00 KEY=K001 DATA=FIRST` / `R2 FS=00 KEY=K002 DATA=SECOND` (out-b1/probe/sr8/seqacc.cob). The stale key value in the record area is the discriminator: had the bare READ bound as Format 2 it would have returned K002 first, which is exactly what the ACCESS DYNAMIC control run of the same program does (out-b1/probe/sr8/dynbare.cob -> `R1 ... KEY=K002`, correct per SR9). (b) record-sequential: out-b1/probe/prevseq/prevseq.cob's forward walk. (c) relative, ACCESS SEQUENTIAL: the covering test.
TEST: tests/conformance/2002/pb140_read_gate.cob -- ORGANIZATION RELATIVE ACCESS SEQUENTIAL, four bare `READ F AT END CONTINUE END-READ` statements walking a three-record file; its header states 'Expected values derived from the rules, per leg' and its .out pins READ1=00 READ2=00 READ3=00 READ4=00 FINAL=00 REC=AAAAAAAA EOF=10. That walk is only producible if NEXT is implied, so the test discriminates -- though its own pinned clause is 9.1.13.7, so the SR8 coverage is incidental rather than named. EDITIONS derivation: the 2023 text carries no edition marker on this clause and Annex E is a 2014-to-2023 delta only (E.2 22) 'READ PREVIOUS statement following an OPEN statement' is its single READ entry, which shows PREVIOUS pre-dates 2023 but dates nothing earlier).
